paper_title: How Knowledge Popularity Influences and Enhances LLM Knowledge Boundary   Perception
caption: The prediction accuracy obtained by performing confidence calibration using knowledge popularity generated from different numbers of examples. Each point represents the average prediction accuracy of the model across three datasets.

model_annotations.Bulgarian:
The provided line chart illustrates how prediction accuracy varies across three large language models — LLaMA 8B, Qwen2, and ChatGPT — as a function of the number of examples (referred to as "shots") used in a confidence calibration procedure. The chart displays three distinct lines, each corresponding to one model, plotted against the number of shots on the horizontal axis and prediction accuracy in percentage on the vertical axis.

The horizontal axis (X-axis) is labeled "Shots" and represents the number of examples used for calibration. It is marked with discrete integer values: 0, 3, 5, and 10. The axis uses a linear scale, and the values are evenly spaced with intervals of 3 between the labeled points (0 to 3, 3 to 5, 5 to 10). The vertical axis (Y-axis) is labeled "Prediction Accuracy (%)" and ranges from 78% to 85%. It uses a linear scale with labeled tick marks at intervals of 1 percentage point, starting from 78 and increasing to 85.

The blue line, representing LLaMA 8B, begins at approximately 77.5% at 0 shots, rises to approximately 77.9% at 3 shots, and then remains relatively flat, ending at approximately 77.8% at 10 shots. This line is marked with solid blue circles and is drawn as a solid line.

The orange line, representing Qwen2, begins at approximately 78.5% at 0 shots, remains nearly constant at approximately 78.4% at 3 shots, and then gradually decreases to approximately 77.8% at 10 shots. This line is marked with solid orange squares and is drawn as a solid line.

The green line, representing ChatGPT, begins at approximately 84.9% at 0 shots and slightly decreases to approximately 84.7% at 3 shots. It then remains constant at approximately 84.7% until 5 shots, after which it slightly decreases to approximately 84.6% at 10 shots. This line is marked with solid green triangles and is drawn as a solid line.
model_annotations.German: The diagram illustrates the prediction accuracy (%) of three language models—LLaMA 8B, Qwen2, and ChatGPT—as a function of the number of examples, or “shots,” used for knowledge popularity generation, ranging from 0 to 10 on the x-axis, which is labeled “Shots” and uses a linear scale with tick marks at intervals of 3. The y-axis, labeled “Prediction Accuracy (%)”, spans from 80 to 85 and also employs a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 1. The blue line with circular markers represents LLaMA 8B, starting at approximately 77.6% at 0 shots and rising to about 78.0% at 3 shots before leveling off near 78.0% at 5 shots and slightly decreasing to around 77.8% at 10 shots. The orange line with square markers represents Qwen2, beginning at approximately 78.5% at 0 shots, remaining relatively flat until 3 shots (still around 78.5%), then declining to about 78.0% at 5 shots and further to approximately 77.8% at 10 shots. The green line with triangular markers represents ChatGPT, which starts at approximately 84.9% at 0 shots and decreases slightly to about 84.7% at 3 shots, remaining nearly constant until 5 shots (still around 84.7%), and then declining to approximately 84.5% at 10 shots.
